text:
Jenna (CSM): OK folks — IronHarbor week1 dry-run happening tomorrow 9am PT. Quick sync: we ran the preflight and hit two blocker-ish items: KMS cross-account policy failing test, and audit logs not flowing to their SIEM via our S3 forwarding. Can we triage before the call?
Raj (Network Eng): I looked at the VPC config — their private subnets have no NAT gateway for the bootstrap host so the CloudTrail delivery -> S3 signed PUT is failing. Quick check: do they want a managed NAT or prefer egress via a proxy?
Jenna (CSM): They prefer proxy for egress (company policy). They mentioned an outbound proxy cluster in DMZ.
Devon (Solutions Eng): OK, proxy means we need VPC endpoints for S3 + CloudTrail or proxy rules allowing PUTs. Suggest: add Gateway endpoint for S3 in the route tables for private subnets and route CloudTrail to the S3 endpoint to avoid NAT/proxy.
Raj (Network Eng): Gateway endpoint approach works. But their route tables currently point to a firewall appliance that blocks AWS endpoint prefix lists. We need firewall rule to allow PL/endpoint traffic to S3.
Omar (Security): KMS side: their CMK policy denies our service account's PutObject (we're using a cross-account role for S3 writes). Error: "AccessDeniedException: Not authorized to use kms:Encrypt" in the deliverer logs. Do we have their CMK ARN?
Jenna (CSM): I have the CMK ARN in the customer doc: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:987654321012:key/3a4b5c6d-xxxx. They said they wanted us to use their key (compliance).
Devon (Solutions Eng): We need to add the Redwood service principal (redwood-inference-prod role) to the key policy or create a grant for the cross-account role. Minimal key policy snippet I suggest they add:
```
{
  "Sid": "AllowRedwoodS3Encrypt",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::555666777888:role/redwood-inference-provisioner" },
  "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey*"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```
Devon (Solutions Eng): (cont) Or we create a short-lived grant from their side — that's usually fastest during cutover.
Raj (Network Eng): Back to audit logs — CloudTrail is configured to deliver to the customer's S3 bucket but bucket policy blocks our delivery role. We need a policy allowing the CloudTrail service principal plus our cross-account put role. Typical bucket policy add: "\"Principal\": {\"AWS\": [\"arn:aws:iam::555666777888:role/redwood-cloudtrail-writer\"]}"
Omar (Security): Two security asks: 1) Key rotation cadence — they want yearly rotation enforced via KMS automatic rotation? If so, we need to ensure our grant workflow tolerates new key versions. 2) S3 lifecycle: audit logs retention 1 year, then glacier. Confirm.
Jenna (CSM): They confirmed 1 year retention and yearly key rotation. They asked if rotation will break our ingestion.
Devon (Solutions Eng): If they rotate the CMK alias to a new key id, grants are still valid for the new key only if created for the new key. Best path: use an alias in policies and have them create a key rotation automation that also recreates the grant to our role, OR we ask them to enable automatic rotation on the same CMK so the key id remains and rotation uses key material (AWS-managed rotation on the CMK). We'll propose: enable automatic rotation on CMK + maintain grant.
Raj (Network Eng): Firewall/NAT action items before the dry-run: 1) Allow endpoint prefix lists for S3 in perimeter firewall; 2) Add a route for the S3 gateway endpoint to private route tables; 3) Ensure proxy ACLs allow PUT to s3.amazonaws.com if they keep proxy. I'll send a small commands snippet for route table check.
Raj (Network Eng): `aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0abc1234` then verify routes contain `com.amazonaws.us-west-2.s3` via endpoint
Jenna (CSM): I'll update the runbook with the firewall change request and ping their infra lead (ingrid@ironharbor.com).
Omar (Security): Also add CloudTrail data events enabled for S3 and Lambda for the Redwood role. We should see object-level events so we can correlate delivery failures.
Devon (Solutions Eng): For SIEM forwarding: are they using Splunk Heavy Forwarder or a managed SIEM? If Splunk, we can use Kinesis Firehose from S3 notifications or their collector pulling. Any preference?
Jenna (CSM): They use Splunk HEC pulling from S3 via Firehose -> Kinesis -> Splunk. Currently the Firehose role can't read the bucket due to lack of `s3:GetObject` permission.
Devon (Solutions Eng): So actions: update bucket policy to allow their firehose role & our cloudtrail writer role; add `s3:GetObject` to the reading role; verify bucket notifications for ObjectCreated.* to trigger Lambda that pushes to Firehose if needed.
Raj (Network Eng): Quick timeline ask: Can we get firewall rule change scoped to allow S3 endpoints today? Ops estimates 3 hours. If not, we'll rely on proxy path and add NAT as fallback.
Jenna (CSM): I'll ask Ingrid for approval now.
infra-bot: runbook updated: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-9923 — "IronHarbor Week1 Dry-run Prep" (edited)
Jenna (CSM): Next: test plan for tomorrow — 1) CMK grant applied by customer, 2) Bucket policy updated, 3) Endpoint/routes in place, 4) CloudTrail delivery succeeds (we should see a PutObject event), 5) Firehose can read & forward. Who can own smoke test 4?
Devon (Solutions Eng): I'll own 4 and 5. I'll run a manual CloudTrail put test once they claim the bucket policy change.
Omar (Security): I'll validate the CMK policy and simulate `Encrypt` via `aws kms generate-data-key --key-id alias/their-cmk` from the cross-account role to confirm grants.
Raj (Network Eng): I'll double-check route tables and firewall rule propagation starting now.
Jenna (CSM): Thanks — I'll compile these actions and send an agenda to IronHarbor. Quick question: any blockers that would justify postponing the dry-run?
Devon (Solutions Eng): Not if they can apply the bucket policy + CMK grant today. If those are delayed, we should postpone.
Jenna (CSM): Got it. I'll update schedule based on Ingrid's reply. :thumbsup:
Ingrid (ironharbor): (in customer thread) we'll push the bucket policy change at 3pm PT and confirm CMK grant by 5pm.
Jenna (CSM): Perfect — thanks Ingrid. We'll keep the 9am slot unless anything changes.
Devon (Solutions Eng): I'll prepare a short failure rollback checklist: remove cloudtrail log delivery, revoke temporary grants, and fall back to a Redwood-managed bucket if needed.
Omar (Security): Add alerting: if CloudTrail PutObject fails 3x in 15m, trigger PagerDuty to oncall-security.
Jenna (CSM): Noted. I'll add alerts to the runbook. See you all tomorrow.
